Hoerire/FlymeFreeform.body:
Bring Meizu's Flyme small-window interaction to ColorOS: swipe diagonally inward and upward from a bottom corner of the screen to bring up a fan-shaped menu, slide to the target and release to immediately open it as a freeform floating window.

## Preview

## Features

### Fan menu

- **Trigger**: swipe diagonally inward and upward from a bottom corner; options: left and right, left only, right only
- **Stay active**: the menu stays open after release, so you can keep sliding to pick an item
- **Range and size**: corner detection zone 24–160 dp, icon hit radius 40–140 dp, icons 32–56 dp; the screen previews live while dragging
- **Pause**: landscape and game mode only pause triggering; it resumes automatically after exiting

### Fan apps

Up to six items; apps, clones, sidebar tools and quick entries can be mixed. Long-press and drag to reorder; sliding over a slot enlarges it as feedback, and releasing launches it.

### “More” panel

The “More” item at the end of the fan is taken from the smart sidebar’s “All”, and supports favorites, recents and name search; it closes automatically when the fan is opened.

### Small-window interaction

- **Close small window**: tap outside the window, double-tap outside, or tap the window’s bottom bar
- **Window count**: concurrency limit raised to 1–5
- **Auto-close windows**: when the limit is exceeded, the oldest window is closed instead of being collapsed into an edge bubble
- **Edge keep-alive**: same edge docking as Flyme; apps collapsed into an edge bubble keep running in the foreground
- **Long-press mute**: long-pressing a floating window mutes only that app; long-press again to unmute; other apps are unaffected
- **Lift restrictions**: apps that originally didn’t support freeform windows can also be opened
- **Quick swipe up**: swiping up on the bottom bar switches to mini form
- **Lightweight open**: decides by scenario whether to open as a small window — notification center, notification banners, control center, open app, login authorization, app sharing, system-initiated sends, copy link
- **Disable floating**: apps in the list are left unchanged whether they are launched by others or launch others

### Edge keep-alive

After a window collapses into an edge bubble, the app does not enter pause and keeps running according to its foreground state. The system would normally move the task to the background at this moment and notify the app to pause; the module intercepts this step while the bubble still appears as usual. Games can keep rendering and idle, and resource downloads and updates are not interrupted.

Only applies to tasks in the bubble; when there is no bubble, it does not intervene and other apps are unaffected. Apps in the bubble continuously use CPU and GPU, so battery drain and heat will increase; turn off the switch when not needed.

When the screen is locked, windows are hidden in the system’s original way and do not expand on their own; after unlocking, they can be opened normally from the bubble or the wheel.

While an app is in the bubble it gains system background exemption (power-saving whitelist) at the same time, so after locking the screen, new network requests and episode auto-play are no longer blocked by background restrictions; the exemption is revoked automatically upon leaving the bubble.

### Long-press mute

Long-press a small window or mini window for about 0.5 seconds to mute only **the app that owns the current window**; long-press again to unmute. Muting uses the system’s per-app volume channel, so it does not mute the media stream as a whole and does not affect other apps in use at the same time.

Trigger conditions: the press position must fall within the visible area of the current floating window, and displacement must not exceed 40px; normal dragging and resizing do not trigger it by mistake.

### Free sharing

Lifts the official whitelist restriction; standard controls and web pages within the main window can both be long-pressed to drag up text and images (ColorOS 17 only).…

MuLiuSaMa/MeowCode.body:
A local programming Agent desktop app whose **architecture can be changed as you like**.

Electron + React handle the UI. The Agent core runs in a local HTTP/SSE service, and the UI and core communicate only through an event stream, so the core can run alone, be swapped alone, or be rewritten alone without affecting the UI.

## Highlights

-   **Core and UI fully decoupled**: `pnpm dev:server` runs the core standalone without Electron; any HTTP client can connect.
-   **Not a black box**: tool calls, approvals, compression, and caching policies are all plain TypeScript in `src/agent/`. Changes take effect immediately, with no packaging magic.
-   **Taking tokens seriously**: server-side native compression + local summarization + three-layer governance of tool output + output budget pre-checks, so long sessions are less likely to crash.
-   **The desktop is not just a shell**: terminal, browser, email, file preview, Git, diff review, and the floating island all live in the same window, so you don't have to switch back and forth between editor and terminal.
-   **Local first**: sessions, keys, and logs stay on your machine. Once a key enters memory, it is erased from environment variables and never written to disk.

## Features

**Model access**

-   Supports three protocols: Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions, and OpenAI Responses.
-   Built-in catalog of common providers (DeepSeek, Kimi, Tongyi, Zhipu, OpenRouter, etc.), and fully customizable.
-   Model capability profiles: thinking budget tiers, prompt cache TTL / breakpoints, PDF and image input gating.
-   Automatic provider failover (timeout / rate limit / 5xx); abnormal exits don't interrupt the turn.

**Tools and approvals**

-   Files and search: `list_dir` / `read_file` / `glob` / `grep` (built-in ripgrep) / `write_file` / `edit_file` / `multi_edit`.
-   Command execution: `run_command` runs PowerShell (5.1 and 7 behavior aligned). Exit codes are reported honestly, and failures are no longer treated as success. There is no stdin channel, so interactive commands fail immediately instead of hanging until timeout. Color codes and progress noise are stripped at the capture layer. Overlong output keeps the head and tail, so errors are not cut off with the tail. High-risk commands get a risk warning.
-   Browser: `browser_navigate` / `browser_click` / `browser_type` / `browser_screenshot` / `browser_snapshot` / `browser_back` / `browser_reload`. It drives the guest webContents of embedded tabs directly, and snapshots include only visible, interactable elements (up to 200).

# AdbHide-Kernel

[Simplified Chinese](https://github.com/SampleBlazkness/AdbHide-Kernel/blob/HEAD/README.md) | [English](https://github.com/SampleBlazkness/AdbHide-Kernel/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

It consists of three modules: the Manager (an LSPosed module), the kernel module, and the Zygisk module.

1. **Manager (LSPosed) layer**: Rewrites the developer options, USB debugging, and wireless debugging settings that apps read so they appear disabled, applied globally (can be selectively enabled or disabled). If the Manager is not installed or fails to inject at boot, the kernel module and Zygisk module also stop working.
2. **Kernel layer**: For apps on the list, hides adbd's socket, listening ports, `/proc/net` entries, and properties.
3. **Zygisk layer**: Replaces the property memory mapping inside target processes, covering apps that bypass the Java layer and read property files directly.

## Full Installation

1. Run `uname -r`, choose the kernel module from the table below, and install it in your root manager.
2. Install `AdbHide-native-v*.zip`.
3. Install `AdbHide-*.apk`, grant root in your root manager, enable AdbHide in LSPosed, and check "System Framework" in its scope (recommended; the scope already includes it and it is checked by default).
4. Reboot.
5. Open AdbHide, tap "Manage apps," check the apps you want to hide, and save to apply.

> Steps 1, 2, and 3 can be done in any order.
> If you are afraid of bricking your device and install only the Manager to spoof system settings, this is not recommended, because other modules already do more at the pure LSPosed level, such as DuckUSB and "I'm Not a Developer."

fakeyanss/jt808-server-go.body:
# jt808-server-go

> Terminal access service for JT/T 808 / JT/T 1078 / Subiao active safety. One protocol core, supporting Standalone single-process and Cluster multi-role deployment.

## Project Positioning

jt808-server-go is a vehicle terminal access service written in Go, aimed at users of self-built vehicle supervision platforms, device access gateways, and protocol integration tools.

It consolidates terminal registration and authentication, location and alarms, active safety attachments, audio/video signaling, and media data into a single protocol core. Business data can use memory, SQLite, or MySQL depending on deployment scale. When access volume is small, one process can serve terminals; as access grows, it can be split by role into 808 gateway, control, 1078 media, and attachment nodes, with the protocol core unchanged.

The project does not provide a frontend console, only a JSON API; the business UI, account system, and tenant model are built by the user.

## Features

- **Protocol core decoupled from deployment shape**: the same encoding/decoding, packet splitting, reply pairing, and business processing run either as a Standalone single process or split by role.
- **Three-version 808 access**: compatible with message header and body differences across JT/T 808-2011/2013/2019, selecting field widths and encoding per version.
- **Active safety closed loop**: receives Subiao `0x1210/0x1211/0x1212` and file streams, supporting retransmission, disk persistence, object storage, progress queries, and file download.
- **1078 signaling and media**: covers live streaming, terminal playback, resource queries, and FTP upload signaling; receives RTP on dedicated UDP/TCP ports, restores H.264, G.711A/U, and ADTS AAC; supports HTTP-FLV playback, RTMP restreaming, platform recording segmentation, and coverage queries.
- **Cluster role split**: five binaries — `jt-signal`, `jt-control`, `jt-media`, `jt-attachment`, `jt-server-standalone` — with fixed roles and independent probes; the control plane exclusively owns metadata, and the data plane does not connect to the business database.
- **Session directory and downlink routing**: gateways claim sessions with control via `0x0102`; in `directory` mode, the owning gateway is located by phone number, so cross-node downlink no longer depends on a fixed entry point.
- **Optional reliability semantics**: uplink chooses `best_effort` or `at_least_once` per message category; the downlink outbox supports idempotency, leases, backoff, expiry, and redelivery, with at-least-once semantics.
- **Verifiable access pipeline**: includes a built-in terminal simulator supporting out-of-order packets, dropped fragments, malformed frame injection, and UDP access; `make smoke` runs end-to-end scenarios against real binaries.

posanbu/Kaguya.body:
## 🌙 Meet Kaguya

Kaguya (辉夜) is a chat agent based on large language models. It aims to be a friendly, natural AI group member: chatting casually together, teasing each other, replying at the right moments, and leaving room for listening and silence.

Kaguya continuously perceives its surroundings, places fragmentary information back into the unfolding context to understand it, then decides whether, when, and how to interact naturally. Through shared experiences, it gradually builds memories and personality.

Supporting this goal is an **event-driven framework**. A continuously running Agent can connect to multiple scenarios such as group chats, private chats, live streams, tools, or devices. New information arriving is an opportunity to re-observe the environment, not an automatic trigger to start a question-and-answer round. A unified information foundation stores traceable facts, and each module then selects the full context according to its own responsibilities, rather than treating a single incoming message as the entire context.

## 💡 Why it is designed this way

### Continuous perception: new information is not a new turn

Information in group chats and live streams is often fragmentary and continuous, and it isn't always directed at Kaguya. Chat messages, scheduled facts, background task results, or device feedback can all serve as a wake-up. They signal that "the environment has changed," but they do not automatically create a turn that must be completed, nor do they promise a generated reply or long-term memory.

Multiple wake-ups can be understood together, and one action can be based on several changes. "Continuous perception" here does not mean continuously calling the model. It means the system can be woken by relevant information and continue observing from the point it has already processed.

### Natural interaction: actions do not map one-to-one to messages

Kaguya first understands what is happening, then chooses `message`, `wait`, or `silent`. When someone in the group is still adding to a question, it can keep waiting. When there is no new value to add to the conversation, it can stay silent. When a time-consuming tool finishes, it can continue earlier work based on the returned result.

Therefore, receiving a piece of information and taking an action are two different things. Input and output can proceed at their own pace. "Dual-track" is only an implementation philosophy that helps design module boundaries. It is not a product concept users need to understand, and it does not presuppose a general concurrency protocol.

### One Agent, connecting multiple scenarios

Information from different entry points flows into a unified information foundation. Each module subscribes to the facts it cares about, processes them, and then publishes results. Persisted information atoms store evidence and sources. They can wake modules, but they do not automatically equal the complete context a module needs to understand.

This allows **entry points and capabilities to evolve separately**. Adding a chat platform can reuse existing memory and decision modules, and adding a capability can serve multiple entry points. What is unified is Kaguya's identity, operational facts, and capabilities. Specific observation and action still select context according to scenario scope, preserving boundaries for people, group chats, and permissions, and avoiding mixing information across different scenarios.

For contributor-oriented terminology, module checklists, and the current implementation mapping, see [Continuous Agent design principles](https://github.com/posanbu/Kaguya/blob/HEAD/docs/developers/continuous-agent.md) and [Runtime architecture](https://github.com/posanbu/Kaguya/blob/HEAD/docs/developers/architecture.md).

# comfyui-zh-tag-autocomplete

Chinese tag autocomplete for ComfyUI: type **Chinese directly** into a node's text box and matching Danbooru English tags pop up for you to pick from. You can also **translate** an entire Chinese prompt into tags in one click. Chinese terms that aren't in the dictionary (including full sentence descriptions) are translated with Google or DeepSeek, which suits models like Anima that understand natural language.

For the SD WebUI / Forge version, see [sd-webui-zh-tag-autocomplete](https://github.com/wangjue520/sd-webui-zh-tag-autocomplete).

- Includes **125,778** tags with 50 or more Danbooru images, each with a Chinese name and several Chinese synonyms
- General tags include colloquial phrasings, e.g. `head_out_of_frame` ← "head out of frame" / "head outside the frame" / "head not captured"…; fuzzy matching also applies when phrasing isn't an exact match
- Characters and works support translated names, short names and community nicknames, e.g. `saber_(fate)` ← "my king" / "ahoge king" / "knight king"

---

## Installation

**ComfyUI-Manager**: enter `https://github.com/wangjue520/comfyui-zh-tag-autocomplete` under "Install via Git URL"

**git**:

```bash
cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/wangjue520/comfyui-zh-tag-autocomplete
```

**Archive**: download the ZIP, extract it to `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/`, and make sure the structure is `custom_nodes/comfyui-zh-tag-autocomplete/__init__.py`.

Restart ComfyUI after installing. No Python dependencies need to be installed.

---

## Usage

### 1. Chinese autocomplete

In any node's multi-line text box (such as CLIP text encode), type Chinese. After the input method commits the text, candidates pop up:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ↑ / ↓ | Move selection up / down |
| PageUp / PageDown | Jump 5 items |
| Enter / Tab | Insert the selected tag |
| Esc | Close the candidates; this segment keeps its Chinese (no real-time translation when typing a comma) |
| Mouse click | Insert that tag |

- Candidates are sorted by exact match → prefix match → contains → fuzzy match; within each level, tags are ordered by Danbooru image count, highest first
- Category colors: blue = general, green = character, purple = work, orange = meta tag, red = artist, cyan = machine translation

# SoloPDF

Website: https://solopdf.doaipm.com · GitHub: https://github.com/zhitongblog/solopdf

Free · ad-free · local-first cross-platform PDF reader. **Highlights are notes**: every highlight you make in a PDF is automatically saved as a companion Markdown file. [SoloMD](https://solomd.app) can open it, RAG can search it, and git can version it.

solo suite members: SoloMD (Markdown) · SoloPDF (PDF). These are two independent apps that interoperate through Markdown files.

## Why

PDF readers on Windows either show ads (Adobe/Foxit/WPS) or make do with Edge.
SoloPDF: opens instantly, zero ads, zero telemetry (update checks can be fully disabled), free forever.

## Core features (v1.0)

- **Highlights → `.annotations.md`**: annotations include page deep links (`solopdf://`). Click one to jump back to the exact position in the original. Anchoring is triple-layered (text fingerprint > page number + coordinates). After the PDF is updated, highlights relocate automatically; if relocation fails, they are greyed out and degrade gracefully, and the body text is never lost.
- **Edit annotations in SoloMD**: the companion file is plain Markdown, and external edits take effect when the editing window regains focus.
- Streaming load for large files: a 157MB / 1048-page file cold-starts in ~1s, and virtual scrolling keeps memory constant.
- Full-text search (CJK-friendly, NFKC normalization, which even handles the Kangxi radical code-point pitfall in PDFs exported by Skia).
- Outline tree / thumbnails / bookmarks / multiple tabs / reading position memory (after a file is moved, it is found again via content hash).
- **Annotations aren't limited to highlights**: underline / strikethrough / squiggly underline / sticky-note pins / **area-select screenshots**. Screenshots are stored in `<document name>.annotations.assets/`, and the companion MD references them as `` (SoloMD, GitHub, and any Markdown reader display the image directly).
- **Import annotations from other apps**: highlights, underlines, strikethroughs, squiggly underlines, sticky notes (including replies), text boxes, freehand drawings, rectangles, ellipses, lines/arrows, and polygons left in a PDF by Acrobat / Preview / PDF Expert / Zotero / Foxit. On open, you're prompted to import the companion file in one click. Source excerpts, authors, dates, and colors are preserved; the import is reversible; repeat imports don't duplicate; after import, the original annotations are no longer drawn by the PDF. The PDF itself is not modified.
- **Export a copy with standard PDF annotations**: writes the annotations from the companion file as real PDF annotations, visible in Preview / Acrobat / Foxit. The original file is never modified.
- **View**: rotate the whole document or a single page (one click from the toolbar), single / two-page spread, continuous scroll / single-page paging, …
